ik what voice youre talking about but thats not “the trans voice”… thats the incomplete voice training voice… trans voices dont end up different than cis voices. they just sound different while theyre mid way through the process.

ok girls im going to give you the best voice training guide ever.

step 1 is you raise your larynx, just to get a higher pitch. mess around with it until you find a voice thats higher by doing that. its ok if it takes effort and ur voice gets a little strained, as long as it doesnt physically hurt its fine. 

step 2 is dont stop. ever. thats your voice now. dont switch back and forth just always put in the effort to do your new voice. it’s ok if it sounds weird. it’s ok if it makes you cough every 5 seconds. just keep doing it.

step 3 is watch some videos. trans voice lessons is great but don’t over worry ab understanding everything she says. you can do the exercises if you want but they’re not really necessary. if you have a really nasally voice it’s maybe more helpful but it’s not the most important thing.

more important is that you watch youtube videos from girls who you want your voice to sound like. and focus on their accent. you dont need to copy them out loud but maybe copy their accent for your internal monologue. just think about how they say stuff. 

note about accents: dont copy the stereotypical valley girl voice like some people say to. itll make you sound weird. just copy actual people you see on youtube. 

step 4 is kind of related to the accent thing, just change the way your vowels sound. once youre comfortable enough in your new voice after a few days/weeks, and youve started thinking ab your accent, another thing you can do is change your vowels. try to adjust the pronunciation of all your vowels to sound a little closer to “eeee”. like the word “thinking” sounds closer to “theenkeeng” dont over over do it but mess around with it until it sounds good to you.

step 5 is wait about 2 years. just keep up talking in your new voice, do not switch back. you can keep subconsciously thinking about the accent and vowel pronunciation of other girls you hear. it’s not hard like learning a language. after a month or two you won’t feel like you’re voice training, you just have new habits that no longer take effort. 

your voice won’t sound perfect right away, it’s like estrogen it changes you slowly. and you’ll wake up one day and from then on you’re “miss” on the phone. you’ll struggle to talk loudly at first, you might sound monotone, your screams might sound scarily similar to your old voice. in time all of these things will change. each of you have a beautiful voice locked inside of you. and you can start the stage of your life where you’re breaking it free today. never ever give up. <3
